question: The Quit India Resolution was passed during which session of the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Session**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Resolution was passed during the **Bombay Session of the Indian National Congress** held on **8 August 1942**.
 
• This session was presided over by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time.
 
• The resolution, also known as the **"August Kranti"**, marked the beginning of the Quit India Movement against British rule in India.
 
• The movement called for immediate independence of India and was characterized by the slogan **"Do or Die"**, given by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The British government reacted swiftly by arresting top Congress leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel, effectively crippling the movement's leadership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement (1942):**

 
 
• It was a mass protest demanding an end to British rule in India during World War II.
 
• The movement was non-violent in principle but saw instances of violent clashes with the British authorities.
 
• The British government described it as the most serious revolt since the 1857 uprising.
 
• Despite the suppression, it significantly strengthened Indian unity and paved the way for independence in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Key Leaders:**
 
 
• Although Mahatma Gandhi was the central figure, other leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, and Aruna Asaf Ali played vital roles.
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali became known as the "Heroine of the Quit India Movement" for hoisting the Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Bombay Session:**
 
 
• The session demonstrated the Indian National Congress's unified demand for complete independence.
 
• It marked a shift from earlier demands for dominion status to a clear call for outright independence.
 
 
 
• **Impact on British Rule:**
 
 
• The movement created immense pressure on the British, who had to divert resources during World War II to suppress the unrest in India.
 
• It showcased the Indian people's determination for self-rule and contributed to the eventual withdrawal of British rule in 1947.
